item.title: Federal Funding Update
item.description:
Dear Valued Stakeholder,

By any measure, the last 20 months have been among the most challenging in our lifetimes.  In this season of Thanksgiving, we want to thank you for your tireless work in helping Columbus battle COVID-19 and the economic and human crises that surround it.  Together, we have held our community intact, but we also know the social fabric has worn thin and existing disparities are clearer than ever.

Your organization requested American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding to continue – and, perhaps, expand – your work.  Again, we thank you for your ongoing commitment to our residents and want you to know we are giving your proposal careful review as we look to make strategic budget decisions.  While looking toward the future, we feel it’s also important to reflect on what we’ve been able to accomplish to date.

Last year, we received $157 million in CARES Act dollars with the requirement to spend them on needs directly related to the pandemic by the end of 2020.  Almost half of those funds went to food, emergency shelter, rental, utility and small business assistance to help Columbus weather the storm.  As the pandemic ebbed and flowed, some community needs changed and new challenges emerged.  The labor market tightened, the supply chain slowed and child care became scarce while the basic needs of food and safe, affordable housing never waned.  Ultimately, all of the CARES Act dollars were allocated.

This year, we were awarded nearly $40 million in federal stimulus to provide emergency rental assistance, all of which has been allocated.  We then received $93.5 million in ARPA dollars, and while the deadline to spend it is not until 2026, nearly half has been directed toward our community’s most pressing needs:

  • Programming to engage our young people, keep them safe and help them learn and grow
  • Incentives to provide high-quality child care so parents can return to work
  • Small business support for companies that continue to struggle in an uneven economy

Roughly $40 million of our first ARPA allocation remains, but our community’s needs are many.  In addition to your proposal, we have approximately $119 million in outstanding funding requests.  What’s more, while the city’s financial position is relatively strong, the future of remote work threatens income tax receipts which are the lifeblood of the city’s budget.  While we remain committed to putting ARPA dollars back into the community, one of the key factors in making funding decisions is the ability to sustain programs once federal stimulus dollars are depleted.  Additionally, we will soon release the Recovery and Resiliency Advisory Committee recommendations which will inform strategic investment of ARPA funding and help align city spending with investments made by the county, Columbus City Schools and our suburban counterparts who have also received hundreds of millions in ARPA dollars.

We will be following up with you in the New Year to further discuss the status of your funding proposal, but we want to, again, express our deepest gratitude for your ongoing commitment to our great city.

Yours in service,

Andrew J. Ginther, Mayor                            Shannon G. Hardin, President
Columbus                                                        Columbus City Council
